implementation.name: SWI-Prolog
implementation.version_scope: Documentation as checked on 2026-10-13; no latest-version claim.

fit.text: Logic queries over facts and rules using SWI-Prolog.

prerequisites.text: Learn terms, unification and query evaluation rather than assignment-based execution.

execution.text: Load a .pl source file into a SWI-Prolog session and submit goals.

behavior.text: Queries may find multiple solutions; fact databases are different from imperative programs.

tooling.text: The interactive session and manual support loading, debugging and documentation.

maintenance.text: Choose the SWI-Prolog version and optional packages with their native dependencies.

costs.text: The core uses Simplified BSD; GMP and optional readline components have separate terms.

example.code:
parent(ada, bob).
parent(bob, clara).
grandparent(X, Z) :- parent(X, Y), parent(Y, Z).
example.run_instructions: Load family.pl in SWI-Prolog, then query grandparent(ada, Who).

implementation.name: CPython 3
implementation.version_scope: Python 3 tutorial and CPython software license; third-party interpreters and packages are separate.

sources.label: Python software and documentation license stack

fit.text: Scripting, application development and extending existing applications; native extensions provide an integration path.

prerequisites.text: The official tutorial expects basic programming knowledge. Start with expressions, control flow and functions before modules.

execution.text: Install a Python 3 interpreter and run the .py script; the tutorial supports interactive experimentation.

behavior.text: Python is dynamically typed and interpreted; C or C++ extensions can add functions and data types.

tooling.text: Use the interpreter, built-in objects and standard library documentation; third-party modules extend this foundation.

maintenance.text: Keep interpreter and extension dependencies aligned; a Python extension written in C or C++ adds another toolchain.

costs.text: The interpreter and standard library are freely available; additional modules and external services require their own evaluation.

example.run_instructions: With Python 3 installed, run python3 hello.py on systems using that command, or py -3 hello.py with the Windows Python launcher.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.
